subject: Exploring SKU tiling for 3-tier plan — reseller margin implications
messages:
From: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cloudretailer.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-17T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: SKU tiling question for our 3-tier private offer

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for taking the time earlier. We’re mapping how your SKUs would translate into our storefront and want to avoid confusion for customers while preserving reseller economics. Two quick asks from my side:

1) Example of how SKU tiling (i.e., small/med/large list-price buckets) affects reseller netback if we apply a 7% reseller commission plus a volume-based rebate.
2) Any constraints on how AWS/GCP/Azure marketplaces meter list price vs. post-commission amounts (we need clarity for our billing team).

If you can send a short example worksheet and call out operational friction points (tax handling, invoice flows, Marketplace PO timing), that’d be great.

We’re eyeing a Q4 private offer, target start 2027-01-01. HubSpot deal id is DEAL-12345.

Best,
Jordan
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Cloud Retailer Inc.

P.S. CC’ing our finance alias for visibility (they may pipe in with tax/form asks).

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cloudretailer.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-17T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU tiling question for our 3-tier private offer

Jordan — thanks, good questions. Attaching a short worksheet (sku-tiling-proposal.xlsx) and our pricing guideline summary (redwood-pricing-guidelines.pdf). High level thoughts below: 

- SKU tiling approaches we recommend:
  * Flat list-price tiers (Simple). Pros: predictable storefront presentation. Cons: can compress reseller margin if large customers are bucketed but usage skews high.
  * Volume-tiered discounts (Metered tiers). Pros: protects list-price anchoring; enables overage buckets. Cons: requires clear metering on marketplace meter or usage report.
  * Bundle SKUs (slot + support). Pros: preserves list-price while shifting margin to add-ons. Cons: more SKUs to manage in marketplace.

- Reseller economics example (worksheet): we modeled a 7% reseller commission (calculated on gross invoice) + end-of-quarter rebate tiers (1–3% based on attainment). The netback waterfall in the sheet shows effective netback across usage profiles.

- Marketplace metering: in AWS/GCP/Azure private offers the list price is what customers see and is what Marketplace meters for usage-based SKUs. Reseller commissions typically are paid out-of-band (contractual) and do not change the metered list price; that means your billing reconciliation must account for the commission as a downstream settlement rather than a modification of the SKU price.

- Tax & invoice flows: marketplaces have differing VAT/sales tax handling; we recommend routing commissions as separate AR credits or rebate invoices so the marketplace invoice remains clean. I flagged common friction points in the PDF.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm target committed volume by SKU bucket (quick numbers are fine).
2) Ben can run a margin-waterfall example with our finance assumptions.
3) We schedule a 30-minute ops call (marketplace billing + procurement) to align on invoice flows.

Happy to jump on a call this week.

— Lukas Meyer
Senior Strategic Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cloudretailer.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU tiling question for our 3-tier private offer

Jordan — looping in a quick margin example (attached: margin-waterfall-example.csv). A few operational clarifications from our side: 

- We recommend structuring the private offer to use a single metered SKU per product family and expose list-price tiers via Marketplace pricing rules. That minimizes catalog complexity.
- For reseller pay, best practice we’ve landed on is: marketplace invoices customer at list price; reseller invoice/credit runs monthly as a separate ledger entry. This simplifies tax treatment in most regions.
- If Cloud Retailer prefers reseller deduction on the invoice, that requires marketplace-specific passthrough configuration (not always possible) and can delay private offer publication.

Irene — quick Q for Marketplace Ops: will AWS private offers allow us to publish a metered SKU with tiered pricing while still enabling a separate settlement path for reseller commissions? If not, we should flag this as a potential blocker to the Jan 1 start.

Jordan — can you send your estimated bucket volumes (small/med/large) and a contact at procurement so we can surface required W9/TIN or equivalent docs for tax?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-19T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU tiling question for our 3-tier private offer

Jordan / Priya — nice to meet you over email. Quick answers and proposed timeline: 

1) Tax treatment and reseller commissions: Redwood treats reseller commissions as partner expense; we issue rebate/credit memos (separate AR entry). For US tax reporting we will provide a W9 and our EIN on request — attaching basic tax stub in the Drive folder for procurement.

2) Canonical usage reporting: for metered products the marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) provides the supplier usage report; Redwood also emits a usage report from our runtime for cross-checks. Best practice is to reconcile marketplace metered reports against Redwood’s usage exports weekly in the first month, then monthly after stabilizing.

3) Operational constraints: AWS Private Offer publication typically takes 3–5 business days once PO and pricing are finalized; GCP is similar but can require an extra week for quota approvals in some regions. If you require invoice-level commission deductions rather than post-invoice credits, that may add 7–10 business days and requires marketplace ops sign-off.

Next steps
- I’ll update the worksheet with your bucket numbers and run the margin waterfall (Ben) by EOD tomorrow.
- Let’s schedule a 30-minute ops/finance sync for Thursday (Irene will drive Marketplace/Qs). Proposed times: Thu 10/21 09:00 PT or 11:00 PT — which works?
- I’ve uploaded a mutual action plan to: https://redwood.in/mutual-action-plan/DEAL-12345 — feel free to add rows for procurement and billing owners.

Thanks — we’ll aim to get you a finalized private-offer-ready package by Oct 27 if timelines hold.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
